elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Edited 4.1: "unless terminated by the Company or HDI for convenience and without cause upon ninety (90) days written notice" — the Company's convenience right is now express (though it operates against renewal rather than mid-term).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Notice remains ninety (90) days written notice in 4.1; no 30-day right was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered text; 4.2(a)/(c) still run money from the Company to HDI, and the only addition is a cap sentence.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The edit affirmatively grants HDI a convenience-and-without-cause termination right ("terminated by the Company or HDI for convenience and without cause"), the opposite of removing it.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 4.1 as edited: Company may terminate "for convenience and without cause upon ninety (90) days written notice" — within the 60–90 day band.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Added: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments due from the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." Caps the 4.2(a) payment at three months of Section 3.1 fees; 4.2(c) instalment mechanic remains consistent.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The edit gives HDI an express right to terminate "for convenience and without cause upon ninety (90) days written notice" with no words limiting HDI to the end of a term or to non-renewal, and the retained next sentence ("Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated") lets the terminating party pick any Termination Date. The end-of-term limitation is at best implied by the renewal framing and is now contradicted; the drafter must add express words such as "HDI may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term, by preventing renewal".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Same sentence requires ninety (90) days written notice from either terminating Party, including HDI.

reasons: Fallback is incomplete: the redline converts HDI's ambiguous non-renewal right into an express "for convenience and without cause" right on 90 days' notice without any operative limitation to the end of the then-current term, so element 3 fails. Repair by splitting the sentence, e.g. "...unless terminated by the Company for convenience and without cause, or by HDI effective only at the end of the then-current term, in either case upon ninety (90) days' written notice".

The retained sentence "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" now combines with the new express convenience grant to let HDI select a mid-term Termination Date; that ambiguity must be closed for the end-of-term element to hold.

Preferred level is not reached: notice stays at 90 days rather than 30, there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, and HDI retains (indeed gains) a convenience right — correctly acknowledged in the rationale.

The fee cap is well drafted and does reach the fallback on early-termination fees: the Termination Payment is capped at three months of Section 3.1 payments and the 4.2(c) instalment mechanic is left intact.

Minimality fails on one point: extending "for convenience and without cause" to HDI is a change outside the customer-side checklist that expands the counterparty's exit right; only the Company's right needed to be made express.
